content.text:
I've completed a thorough line-by-line review of all target production files (reading the full diffs plus enclosing functions, and cross-checking the CSV parser subclasses, CategoryDropdown, service signatures, and SvelteKit's `resolve`). This is a large but unusually faithful refactor (singleton→DI conversion, helper extraction, shared `resolveCategory`/`pdfExportState` utils, tolerance/sign-convention consolidation). I could not find a high-confidence correctness regression. Below are the candidates that have a concretely nameable failure scenario, ordered by confidence — all are low.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "src/routes/reconciliation/+page.svelte",
    "line": 165,
    "summary": "Reconciliation reload effect no longer reads urlDateFrom/urlDateTo unconditionally; they are only tracked once loadReconciliation() first runs (guarded by result !== null).",
    "failure_scenario": "The old effect read `urlDateFrom`/`urlDateTo` at the top on every run, so they were tracked from the first render. Now they are only read inside `loadReconciliation()`, which the effect skips while `result === null`. If the initial `onMount` load throws (e.g. transient network/RLS error), `result` stays null forever, so the effect never calls `loadReconciliation` and never starts tracking the URL dates — changing the date filter afterward will not reload. (Note: the old code's `if (result !== null)` guard had the same no-reload-after-initial-error outcome, so this is a narrowing of tracking rather than a clear new break.)"
  },
  {
    "file": "src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte",
    "line": 255,
    "summary": "buildCategoryMap now writes an explicit null for uncategorized receipts, whereas the old loop left those keys unset.",
    "failure_scenario": "Old code only set `map[receipt_id]` when `exp.category_id` was truthy, so uncategorized receipts had NO key. `buildCategoryMap` sets every receipt_id to `resolveCategory(...)`, which returns null for uncategorized rows. Any downstream consumer that distinguishes `undefined` (key absent) from `null` — e.g. `receipt_id in categoryMap` or `Object.keys(categoryMap).length` used as a 'how many are categorized' signal — would now see all receipts present. Truthy checks like `{#if categoryMap[id]}` are unaffected. Verify no such key-presence logic exists on this page."
  }
]
```

Notable non-bugs / things I verified as correct:
- All six CSV parser subclasses were correctly updated to the new `finalizeRow(date, vendor, rawAmount, rowNumber, errors[, msg])` signature (no positional-argument shift), and `AmexParser` sets `expensesArePositive = true`. Sign behavior is preserved.
- `CategoryDropdown.svelte` safely handles the now-nullable `color` via `|| DEFAULT_CATEGORY_COLOR`, so `resolveCategory` returning `color: null` won't produce an invalid swatch.
- `resolve()` from `$app/paths` (SvelteKit 2.63) explicitly accepts `PathnameWithSearchOrHash`, so `resolve('/expenses?...')` with query strings is supported — filters are not mangled.
- `ReconciliationService` reconcile/scoring refactor is behavior-preserving (tolerances default to 3 days / 0.01 CAD / 5% FC; CAD and FC confidence bands unchanged; greedy first-available matching preserved). Removed `DuplicateReceiptInfo` import is genuinely unused.
- The transactions refactor actually FIXES a latent bug: the old page passed `{ includeIgnored }` but `TransactionService.list` reads `options.includeExcluded`, so the "Show excluded" toggle was a no-op; the new code passes `includeExcluded: includeIgnored`.
